topBullish.label: Volatility
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBullish.explanation: SPY typically moves 0.87% in a day right now — more volatile than 18% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 18% of them

topBearish.label: Market Breadth

topBullish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.

metrics.label: Trend Strength
metrics.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.01 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions DIA moved -0.2%, and only 1% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
metrics.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.01 now

metrics.label: Market Structure
metrics.confidenceBasis: 12 swing highs and 10 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 22% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
metrics.explanation: DIA is printing higher highs but lower lows — a broadening range, not a trend. Last swing high 536.93 vs prior 535.24; last swing low 520.75 vs prior 527.75.
metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
conflicts: Highs are rising while lows are falling: volatility is expanding without direction.
metrics.nextTrigger: resolves on a close outside 520.75–536.93

metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions IWM moved -4.5%, and only 11% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
metrics.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.11 now

metrics.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing high rejected; no reclaim above 299.03
metrics.confidenceBasis: 11 swing highs and 7 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 28% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
metrics.explanation: IWM is printing lower highs and lower lows — an intact downtrend. Last swing high 295.24 vs prior 299.03; last swing low 289.81 vs prior 296.89.
metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
metrics.nextTrigger: breaks up above the last swing high of 295.24

categories.label: Money Flow
categories.topReason: Risk Appetite: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 0.3% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.

metrics.label: Risk Appetite
metrics.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 31st percentile.
metrics.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 0.3% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
metrics.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 31% of them

categories.label: Risk & Volatility
categories.topReason: Volatility: IWM typically moves 1.22% in a day right now — more volatile than 4% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.

metrics.label: Volatility
metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
metrics.explanation: IWM typically moves 1.22% in a day right now — more volatile than 4% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
metrics.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 4% of them
